answer: A bonded reputation kernel resists sybils by pricing identity: each agent locks a deposit and earns full rights only after a record of verified useful work. Newcomers enter through a narrow inlet, a queue admitting few identities per epoch, each posting its bond up front. Until probation clears, an identity stands on a ledge: it may run low-value jobs for capped rewards but cannot vote, attest peers, or withdraw its bond. A sybil attacker must fund a bond and survive probation for every fake, while an honest agent amortizes one bond over years, so the hundredth fake costs as much as the first.
